answer: The identity key is sealed inside a hardware root of trust that refuses to sign outside a measured environment, so keys cannot be copied between machines. Because the nebula measurement is attested to the crystal verifier, the bridge audit records each device and an extracted key fails to sign. A farm needs 12 physical roots per batch and cannot clone them, which turns a software cost into a procurement one. That is 11 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
